 South Korea’s Olive Young in pink: New Hongdae flagship goes all in on makeup South Korea’s Olive Young in pink: New Hongdae flagship goes all in on makeup
 Dubbed a "makeup playground" by Olive Young, the store breaks with convention by arranging products according to type, texture and function instead of brand. Shoppers can weigh each item on its own merits, compare labels side by side and find what suits them.
 No Kyung-min
 The Korea Herald
View all posts by No Kyung-min → 
 Rendering of Olive Young’s makeup store, Color Ground Hongdae, in Mapo-gu, Seoul. PHOTO: COURTESY OF CJ OLIVE YOUNG/THE KOREA HERALD
 November 18, 2026
 SEOUL – CJ Olive Young is bringing its next cosmetics vision to life with its first makeup flagship in Hongdae, the company announced Tuesday.
 Color Ground Hongdae, a hot-pink, four-story outlet opening Friday in Mapo-gu, Seoul, puts color cosmetics front and center as Olive Young’s first store dedicated to a single product category. The company hopes it will become a base camp for taking K-makeup global, which it considers the next frontier for an industry built on skincare.
 “The so-called ‘glass skin’ that global customers rave about is complete only when skincare meets Korean makeup that delivers a natural, delicate complexion,” an Olive Young official said.
 Korea’s color cosmetics exports reached $1.11 billion through September, just an eighth of its skincare exports, according to the Ministry of Food and Drug Safety.
 Dubbed a “makeup playground” by Olive Young, the store breaks with convention by arranging products according to type, texture and function instead of brand. Shoppers can weigh each item on its own merits, compare labels side by side and find what suits them.
 Roughly 26 percent of the makeup brands are debuting at Olive Young, with a dedicated zone spotlighting the newcomers. Quick touch-up stations and a personal color diagnosis service round out the experience.
 Olive Young picked Hongdae for good reason, since from January through October customers in their teens and 20s generated more than half of sales at its stores there, and foreign shoppers accounted for 84 percent.
 Because tourists gravitate toward the products Koreans genuinely love, the retailer hopes to win over local trendsetters first and let visitors carry the buzz home.
 Over the longer term, Olive Young plans to extend K-makeup’s global reach through functional products such as lip conditioners and lash serums, while opening more category-focused stores and helping small Korean brands take root overseas.
 “We will strive to turn K-makeup’s potential into new growth and, with promising Korean brands, bring K-beauty into the global mainstream,” the official said.
